question: As per Economic Survey 2022-23, what was the students’ enrollment in higher education in India during the year 2020-21?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3. 4.1 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **Economic Survey 2022-23**, the total enrollment of students in higher education in **India** during the year **2020-21** stood at **4.1 crore**.
 
• This data represents the enrollment of students across various higher education institutions including universities, colleges, and standalone institutions in India.
 
• The increase in enrollment reflects the Indian government's efforts to enhance access to higher education through initiatives such as **NEP 2020** and schemes promoting online education.
 
• The Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER) in higher education for students in the 18-23 age group also showed improvement during this period.
 
• This figure aligns with the government's focus on achieving higher literacy and educational standards to support economic and social development in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER) in Higher Education:**

 
 
• The GER refers to the percentage of the eligible age group (18-23 years) enrolled in higher education institutions.
 
• India's GER in higher education improved significantly in recent years, driven by government initiatives such as **Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA)** and the introduction of **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**.
 
• Efforts to improve GER include enhancing infrastructure, promoting online education, and providing scholarships to disadvantaged groups.
 
 
 
• **Key Government Initiatives for Higher Education:**
 
 
• The **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020** aims to achieve a GER of 50% by 2035 in higher education.
 
• Programs such as **SWAYAM**, a platform for online learning, have been launched to increase accessibility to quality education.
 
• Funding initiatives like **RUSA** aim to improve the quality and infrastructure of higher education institutions.
 
 
 
• **Enrollment Trends in Higher Education:**
 
 
• Between 2019-20 and 2020-21, enrollment in higher education institutions witnessed a significant rise, which can be attributed to efforts to reduce dropout rates and improve access.
 
• More women are enrolling in higher education, indicating progress toward gender parity in educational opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Standalone Institutions in India:**
 
 
• Standalone institutions include **medical colleges, engineering colleges, management institutions, and polytechnic institutions** that are not affiliated with universities.
 
• Such institutions contribute significantly to the overall enrollment in higher education in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Survey 2022-23:**

 
 
• The survey provides detailed insights into various sectors, including education, highlighting trends, challenges, and opportunities.
 
• The focus is on improving the education sector to align with global standards and support India's economic growth.
 
• It underscores the importance of increasing access to quality education and enhancing employability through skill development programs.
 
 
 
• **Impact of COVID-19 on Higher Education:**
 
 
• The pandemic accelerated the adoption of **online education platforms**, contributing to increased enrollment numbers.
 
• Government schemes and digital infrastructure improvements played a significant role in ensuring continuity in education.
